THE SIND FACTORIES (ADULT EXEMPTION)
RULES, 1989
[Sind Govt. Gas. Extr. Pt. I, Mar. 23, 1989,
p 364.]
No. L.‑II‑2‑35/76.‑Karachi,---, the 27th
February, 1989.----- With refe rence to this Department's Notification No.
SO‑(L‑II)‑2‑35/76, dated the 1st June, 1988,
published in the Sind Government Extraordinary Gazette, of October 10, 1988,
the Government of Sind, in exercise of the powers conferred by section 43 of
the Factories Act, 1934 (XXV of 1934), are pleased to make the following rules,
namely: ----
1. Short title end commencement.‑--- (1) These rules may be
called the Sind Factories (Adult Exemption) Rules, 1939.
(2) They shall come into force at
once.
2. In these rules unless there is
any thing repugnant in the subject or context :‑‑
(i) "Act" means the Factories Act,
1934;
(ii) "Chief
Inspector" means the Chief Inspector appointed under sub‑section (2)
of section 10;
(iii) "Form" means the form appended to
these rules;
(iv) "Inspector" means the Inspector
appointed under sub‑section.(I) of section 10;
(v) "Section" means the section of the
Act.
3. Persona bolding position of
attperviaion or madagemtnt.‑‑the follow ing persons shall be deemed
to hold position of supervision or man gement in a factory :‑‑ .
(1) Store
Officer. Section Officer, Workshop Superintendent, Departmental Heads. Chief
Engineer, Electrical Engineer. Boiler En gineer, Mechanical Engineer. Technical
Expert E Overseer, Inspectors of Workshops/Engineering Branches, Foreman,
Chargemen, Head Store Keeper. Chemists. Production Officer, Production Manager,
Mainte nance Engineer and Quality Control Officer.
(a) Any other
person who, in the opinion of the Chief Inspector, holds a position of
supervision or management in the factory.
4. Persons bolding confidential
position punch Operators. Machines operators, data preparation operations in
Computer Section, draftsmen, time keepers and production clerks shall be deemed
to be employed in a con8 dential capacity.
5. A list showing the names and
designations of all persons, to whom the provision of sub‑section (1) of
section 43 have teen applied, shall be maintained and, when so required by the
Inspector, produced before hint.
6. Urgent Repairs.‑‑-- When the work in engineering or
other workshop on the repair of plant or other machinery or plant incidental to
or connec ted in the manufacturing process used in manufacturing processes or
on re- pairs in connection with maintenance of a public service, or in toy
factory on the repair of any part of the machinery, Ship or Aircraft or Engines
of Railways, plant or structure of that factory is of such a nature that delay
in its execution would involve‑‑
(1)
substantial interruption to the manufacturing process In any fac tory; or
(2) substantial interruption to a public
service; or
(3) danger to human life or safety;
all adult male workers employed
on such work shall be deemed to be em ployed on urgent repairs within the
meaning of clause (a) of sub‑section (2) of section 43 and shall he
temporarily exempted from the provisions of section 34, 35. 36, 37, 38, 39 and
40 for the period occupied in the comple tion of such repairs subject to the
following conditions :‑‑
(a) that the period of
exemption for any one worker shall not ex ceed fourteen days in any calendar
month;
(b) that no worker shall be
employed for more than fourteen conse cutive days without one full day's
holiday;
(c) that no worker shall be
employed continuously for more than eight hours without rest/interval of at
least one bout;
(d) That a notice stating
the names of workers employed and the precise nature of their work shall be
sent to the Chief Inspector, the Inspector authorized in this behalf and the
Inspector of area concerned within twenty‑four hours of the commencement
of such employment, and a copy of the said notice shall be affixed in n
conspicuous place near the main entrance of the factory be fore the workers pre
put on such work
